basis: Malignant neoplasm of vascular endothelial cells; no additional organ site is universal across this concept.

Clear cell neoplasm arising in the kidney.
Congenital deafness and progressive leukoencephalopathy define the syndrome; progressive visual loss reported in 1/1 assessed patient.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with frequent brain malformations; optic nerve hypoplasia in 30-79%. Cardiac and hearing abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Cystic subtype of basal cell carcinoma arising in skin.
Glycosylation defect with CNS and hepatic disease; coagulopathy 80-99%. Ocular findings (80-99%), bone abnormalities (1/1) and gut dysmotility omitted at cap.
Dopamine transporter dysfunction causes a central movement disorder; no established additional organ damage.
Infertility itself has no axis; multiple non-erupting secondary teeth in 2/2 reported patients establish a dental phenotype within the gastrointestinal axis.
Lysosomal storage disease with neurodegeneration; dysostosis multiplex in 16/16 and hearing loss commonly >=30%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Inherited retinal degeneration with chorioretinal atrophy and visual field loss.
Umbrella concept for diseases of veins; other organ involvement depends on the subtype.
Hyperplastic mucosal polyp arising in the appendix.
Glutathione deficiency causes metabolic acidosis and hemolytic anemia; neurologic impairment affects roughly one-third or more of systemic cases. Retinopathy is uncommon.
Renal cystic disease with progressive dysfunction. Hepatic cysts are common but usually preserve function; clinically significant liver disease is a minority; hypertension is separate.
Anaerobic bacterial infection of the meninges.
Immunodeficiency defines ICF; developmental impairment, anemia/neutrophil abnormalities and malabsorption each occur in 30-79%. Respiratory infections are separate infections.
Iris hypoplasia and glaucoma affect the eye; the neurological ancestor does not establish extraocular disease.
Malignant smooth muscle neoplasm arising in bone; EBV infection is not intrinsic to this concept.
IMPG2-related retinal degeneration with visual loss; associated cataracts remain within the ocular axis.
Congenital heart and upper-limb malformations define this syndrome group.
Sarcoma arising in the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
Secondary increase in red blood cells; the cause of hypoxia does not establish pulmonary or cardiovascular disease in every case.
Cerebral motor injury causes spastic paralysis of one limb; spasticity alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Malignant neoplasm with skeletal muscle differentiation, typically arising in deep soft tissues of the extremities.
